credit assignment: Working out how much each weight contributed to a mistake, so that each one can be corrected by the right amount.
chain rule: When one thing changes a second and the second changes a third, the overall rate is the two rates multiplied. Backpropagation uses it link by link.
blame: This book's nickname for a gradient: how fast the loss goes up when one number goes up a tiny bit.
backward pass: The second half of a training round: start at the loss and hand the blame back through the network, layer by layer.
gradient check: Testing backpropagation by wiggling one weight a tiny bit, measuring how far the loss really moves, and comparing the two answers.
vanishing gradient: When the blame shrinks at every layer on its way back through a deep network, so the earliest layers barely learn.
